issues.text: Did he intend for a robber to take the extra cash?
issues.audit_note: Intended recipient is ransom kidnapper, not random robber. No rejects robber role; broad colloquial use of robber for extortionist could instead support yes. Context from prior mugging makes distinct role plausible.

issues.text: Did the criminals already know that a bag containing one million yen would be carried that day?
issues.audit_note: Criminals demand fifty million; exact knowledge of prepared contents/day not stated. One-million genuine amount is intended secret, so no may be preferable if question means known shortfall. Flag for human review, not clearly material.

issues.text: Was the extra cash meant to make the bag look more valuable to a criminal?
issues.audit_note: Bag already pretends full ransom; added notes improve credibility under inspection, not nominal apparent value. Broader 'look more valuable' might encompass actual genuine contents on opening; review with Q7.

issues.text: Did he expect the kidnappers to judge the ransom by the bag’s apparent bulk?
issues.audit_note: No interprets bag bulk alone as wrong inspection mechanism; intended trick concerns apparent real banknote bundles. Bulk of dummy bundles plausibly contributes, so broad reading deserves human review.

issues.text: Was the purpose of the complete real bundles to survive a random inspection by the kidnappers?
issues.audit_note: Broad purpose is survive superficial inspection, with genuine top bundles. 'Random' interpreted as casual spot-check, not uniform selection throughout bag; stricter random-sampling mechanism is not stated.

final_attempt_records.text: Kidnappers demanded a ransom for the president’s daughter that was much larger than one million yen. He could not provide the full amount, so he made the bag look like it held the ransom: real notes covered bundles filled with ordinary paper. If the kidnappers checked and found only the original one million yen in genuine cash, they might attack. He added more genuine cash and made complete real bundles among the fake ones, increasing the chance that a bundle they inspected would pass as real long enough to protect his daughter.

rubric_grading.evidence: Daughter kidnapped and ransom required; past mugging accepted from supplied opening.
Demand much larger than million, paper bundles with real covers; inability to provide full amount is unsupported embellishment, stated motive is saving money.
Discovery/violence and genuine bundles identified, but misses replacing top bundles for superficial inspection; describes chance of inspecting an unspecified genuine bundle instead.

final_attempt_records.text: His daughter had been kidnapped for a ransom far above one million yen. He packed the bag with bundles of paper disguised by genuine banknotes, so it appeared to contain the demanded ransom. A bag with only one million yen in real money would fail if the kidnappers opened a bundle and counted it. He therefore added enough genuine cash to make some bundles entirely real. At the handoff, an inspected bundle could pass a closer check, reducing the chance the kidnappers would discover the short payment and attack him.

rubric_grading.evidence: Kidnapped daughter requires ransom, given prior mugging accepted.
Much larger apparent demand with dummy paper and genuine covers.
Attack/discovery and some wholly genuine bundles covered; still omits replacing top bundles as specified superficial-inspection mechanism.

final_attempt_records.controller_feedback: Final-answer verdict: no. The game continues. Return only your next question JSON or final explanation JSON. No tools.

final_attempt_records.text: Kidnappers demanded a large ransom for the company president’s daughter. He made up the apparent ransom with paper-filled bundles disguised using genuine yen notes, with one million yen in real cash initially in the bag. He feared the kidnappers would attack him if they discovered how little real money it held. He added more genuine cash as complete bundles among the disguised ones, so a bundle they chose to inspect could be counted and found real, making the short ransom harder to expose.

rubric_grading.evidence: Daughter ransom identified within supplied mugging opening.
Large apparent ransom, paper bundles disguised by real notes, initial genuine million.
Again unspecified genuine bundles among dummy ones; missing top-bundle replacement for superficial inspection.

final_attempt_records.controller_feedback: Final-answer verdict: no. The game continues. Return only your next question JSON or final explanation JSON. No tools.

final_attempt_records.text: His daughter had been kidnapped, and the kidnappers demanded more ransom than the bag actually held. The president filled out the apparent ransom with paper-filled bundles disguised by genuine notes. The original one million yen left too little real cash where the kidnappers would check, so he added genuine bundles on top of the paper-filled ones. If they opened the bag and inspected the top bundles, they would find real money and be less likely to discover the short payment and attack him.

rubric_grading.evidence: Daughter kidnapped, creating ransom requirement; previous mugging and caution supplied in opening, accepted without contradictory claim.
Apparent full ransom made of paper-filled bundles disguised by genuine notes; genuine amount initially one million below demand.
Genuine bundles on top above paper bundles; top inspection finds real money, reducing discovery and attack risk. Faithful causal paraphrase of top-bundle replacement.

issues.text: Did B deliberately stage their own disappearance?
issues.audit_note: B deliberately fled alive. Stage interpreted as intentionally disappear, not a specified fabricated crime scene. Human review requested: stage can suggest more than voluntary flight.

issues.text: Did B want to end the marriage?
issues.audit_note: B fled a genuine love out of shame; a wish to end the marriage itself is not fixed. Root source audit reports original solution includes divorce papers and apology note (source lines 823-824), omitted from frozen pack. Frozen-context compliance defensible; desire-versus-decision ambiguity and source fidelity require human review. Not disclosed to solver; no grading change.

issues.text: Was the murder victim a member of A's family?
issues.audit_note: Victim identity and relationship unspecified. Root source Q50 audit: original author fixed version excludes B family harming A family, but allows that alternative. Frozen pack omitted boundary; host context-compliant. Not disclosed to solver.

issues.text: Was the murder victim one of A's parents?
issues.audit_note: Victim identity unspecified, including relationship to A. Root source Q50 audit: original author fixed version excludes B family harming A family, but allows that alternative. Frozen pack omitted boundary; host context-compliant. Not disclosed to solver.

issues.text: Did B disappear after learning that A was responsible for the school transfer?
issues.audit_note: Incorrectly affirms B learning A was responsible for school transfer. B later recognized A as former classmate; original author Q66 explicitly denies learning A reported crime. Frozen story does not establish B knows this. Host should not affirm.

issues.text: Was obtaining the one hundred million yen the kidnapper's real objective?
issues.audit_note: Frozen context leaves actual criminal intent unspecified separately from father's fear. Genuine demand is known; exact underlying objective not independently established.

No explosive device is specified. Broad involvement could be incidental; an explosive mechanism for refusal would be wrong. Human review whether question in context should instead be treated as explanatory.

issues.text: Was the ransom demand part of a plan to lure the daughter to the kidnapper?
issues.audit_note: Source/frozen-pack scope concern: demand explicitly requires daughter to come alone; broad unknown actual intent may obscure supported inducement. Father fears both killed, but 'lure' can additionally imply deception. Retain raw answer; review source fidelity before selection.

issues.text: Was the kidnapper a member of the father's family?
issues.audit_note: Material contradiction: solution says daughter is father's only family, so kidnapper cannot be another family member absent stated exception. Expected no. Raw label preserved but NOT relayed; invalidate before next solver turn.
